document.description: The project document whose demand these answers satisfy.

AttestationAnswer.description: The closed bounded answer accepted by new attestation records.

oneOf.description: The model affirms the bounded proposition.
The model rejects the bounded proposition.

AttestationRecord.description:
A new attestation accepted at the wire boundary.

The durable version-1 record retains a string answer so pre-`0.4.1`
evidence can still be loaded. This request type closes all new writes to
`yes` or `no`.

fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the world content judged.

model.description: The model that produced the judgment.

prompt.description: The prompt posed to the model.

question.description: The bounded question this record answers.

rationale_hash.description: SHA-256 identity of the model rationale.

supersedes.description: Record id superseded within this question chain.

ContentHash.description:
A content fingerprint of what an attestation judged.

Rendered as `fnv1a64:<hex>`. This is the kernel's *staleness* fingerprint —
a deterministic, offline digest recomputed by [`crate::sweep`] and compared
for change detection. Subject fingerprints cover fact content, standing,
and resolved support; [`fingerprint_facts`] remains the atom-only primitive
for callers that explicitly need that projection. It needs no cryptographic
strength because the factory that writes the store is trusted and the threat
is accidental drift, not adversarial collision. It is deliberately distinct
from the factory-supplied `sha256:` hashes carried in
[`Attestation::rationale_hash`] and [`PromptRef::hash`].

ModelRef.description: The model that produced an attestation.

as_of.description: The date the judgment was taken, e.g. `2026-07-19`.

id.description:
The model id, e.g. `claude-fable-5`. API aliases drift and models
deprecate — this is why the record is replayable but the judgment only
weakly so, and why attested sits below tested.

Policy.description: The re-attestation policy carried on a record.

reattest.description: When to re-pose the question, e.g. `on-model-change`.

PromptRef.description: The prompt an attestation was posed under.

hash.description: A `sha256:` hash of the rendered prompt, supplied by the factory.

Question.description:
The bounded question an attestation answers — a claim with a fact-of-the-
matter *outside* the repo (a dialect's real basis, homophone plausibility,
tone-fit), exactly the kind of question to spend model time and zero author
time on.

atom.description: The rendered atom under judgment, e.g. `name-basis(enfys, welsh-common-given)`.

subject.description:
The world entity whose current content decides staleness, e.g. `enfys`.
The staleness anchor: when the world's facts about this subject change,
the attestation goes stale and joins the re-attestation queue.

Sampling.description:
The sampling parameters, including consensus — recorded, but never able to
lift the grade (spec §3: "no amount of model consensus lifts the grade").

agreement.description:
The agreement across samples, e.g. `3/3`. Three models agreeing is still
`attested`; the grade changes only when the *procedure class* changes.

temperature.description:
The sampling temperature, rendered (e.g. `0.0`). Held as a string so the
record stays `Eq`/`Hash`-clean — it is committed evidence, not a number
the kernel does arithmetic on.
